question: Soap on your hands under the tap. How long should the scrubbing last to clear most of the germs?
answer: At least 20 seconds, the US Centers for Disease Control advise. Soap molecules have one end that clings to fat and one that clings to water; rubbing works them into the greasy film holding germs, and into some viruses' fatty coats, so rinsing lifts it away. Watched in public toilets, people averaged about 6 seconds.
move: When something works by contact, the time spent is the dose.
ask: Which of my quick routines is too short to do what I assume it does?
reference: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Clean Hands: When and How to Wash Your Hands; Borchgrevink, Cha & Kim, Hand washing practices in a college town environment, Journal of Environmental Health 75(8), 2013; WHO, Hand Hygiene: Why, How and When?, 2009
